name: Issue permits to work and lock out equipment
summary: Before anyone works on plant equipment that could move, energise or release pressure, operations isolate it, lock it and issue a signed work permit. A permit coordinator prepares the isolation list, the shift supervisor verifies it, field and control room operators stop and isolate the equipment, test for zero energy and lock the keys in a group box, and the supervisor briefs the crew and issues the permit. When the work ends the crew removes its locks, the permit is cancelled and operators restore the equipment. The work is slowed by the morning queue at the permit desk, by isolation lists that must be written from drawings, and by locks left on by workers who have gone home.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with three converted gas steam units at two Wabamun-area sites run by power engineers on rotating shifts, using an electronic permit-to-work system with paper isolation records.
baseline.notes: Complex group lockout under Alberta OHS Code Part 15 is the normal method for steam plant work. Outage permits follow the same steps in larger batches.

trigger: A permit request arrives in the permit system from routine maintenance or an outage.
end_state: The permit is cancelled, isolations are removed, the equipment is back in service and the record is closed, or the request is deferred.

volume.seasonality: Highest in the spring and fall outage seasons; routine permits are steady through the year.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Thermal planned outages are scheduled in spring and fall when Alberta demand and prices are lower; same estimate as the organisation file's surge for this process.

About 0.75 permits per routine work order (inspections and operator rounds need none, some permits cover several orders) at 1,400 orders a month, plus outage permits; the organisation file's 1,600 assumes 2,000 routine orders. Estimate.

Role title seen on the company's careers site (after the reference period); duties, headcount (about five across the two sites with outage cover) and pay at the field operator level are the author's estimates.
About a third of the 12 shift supervisors' time on the permit desk, revalidation and cancellation; estimate.

roles.title: Field operator (third- or fourth-class power engineer)

evidence.note: Isolation and restoration share of the 55 field operators' time; estimate.
Control-room part of isolation and return to service; estimate.

systems.name: Document management and engineering drawings repository
ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)

steps.name: Review permit request for the next day
steps.description: The permit coordinator opens the day's permit requests in the permit system, checks each against the unit run plan and other open permits for conflicting isolations, and decides whether a stored isolation list can be reused or a new one is needed. Requests that need the unit offline are deferred.

error.defect_description: Conflict with another open permit not noticed.

next.condition: deferred: needs unit outage or conflicts with other work
no stored isolation list for this equipment

evidence.note: A permit coordinator role exists at the Wabamun-area plant (title only seen); the next-day review and the shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write a new isolation list
steps.description: The coordinator traces the equipment on piping and instrument diagrams and electrical single-line drawings, lists every valve, breaker, drain and vent to operate with its required position and lock, and notes stored energy such as pressure, heat or springs. The list is saved for reuse.

error.defect_description: Isolation point missed, such as a backfeed or a bypass valve.

evidence.note: Estimate of drafting time for an isolation list on a steam plant system.

steps.name: Prepare isolation list from template
steps.description: The coordinator copies the stored isolation list for the equipment, checks recent engineering changes and temporary modifications that might change it, and attaches it to the permit with the job hazards from the work order.

error.defect_description: Template is out of date after a plant change.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Verify and authorise the isolation list
steps.description: The shift supervisor, a first-class power engineer, checks the isolation list against the drawings and the current plant line-up, confirms the unit can run with the equipment out, and authorises operators to isolate. Errors go back to the coordinator.

error.defect_description: Verifier misses an error in the list.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.215.1(2): separate activation and verification roles in complex group control

evidence.note: Separate activation and verification roles are required under complex group control.

steps.name: Take equipment out of service from the control room
steps.description: The control room operator starts the standby pump or fan, stops the equipment to be worked on from the DCS, puts it in local or out-of-service mode and confirms that the unit is stable before field isolation starts.

evidence.note: Estimate; equipment must be stopped before isolation (ohs15 s.212).

steps.name: Collect locks and walk to the equipment
steps.description: The field operator prints the isolation list, collects the numbered locks and tags from the lock board and walks or drives within the plant to the equipment, which can be several floors up in the boiler house.
outputs: locks and tags at the job

evidence.note: Estimate of in-plant walking time.

steps.name: Apply isolations, locks and tags
steps.description: The field operator closes and chains valves, opens drains and vents, opens low-voltage disconnects and attaches a numbered lock and tag to each isolation point in the order on the list, ticking each one off.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.212: energy isolated with secured energy-isolating devices before work

evidence.note: Isolation requirement; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Rack out breaker and prove dead
steps.description: An instrument and electrical technician in arc-flash clothing racks out the 4,160 V or 480 V breaker at the switchgear, locks the cubicle and proves the motor circuit dead with a tester before handing the key to the operator.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.212 and s.213: isolation and verification of electrical energy

evidence.note: Share of permits needing a medium-voltage rack-out and the minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Lock keys in box and post isolation record
steps.description: The operator puts the keys of all isolation locks in the group lock box, locks it, and posts the signed isolation record at the work site and in the permit system so the crew can see what is isolated.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.215(3): group control, keys secured and report posted at the work site

steps.name: Test for zero energy
steps.description: The operator tries to start the equipment locally, reads pressure and temperature gauges, bleeds residual pressure and confirms that nothing moves or flows. A passing valve or a live circuit sends the isolation back for correction.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.213: test that the equipment is inoperative before work

next.condition: passing valve or residual energy found

evidence.note: Verification requirement; failure share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue permit and brief the crew
steps.description: The shift supervisor reviews the verified isolation, signs the permit, and holds a short pre-job briefing with the crew lead on hazards, isolations, gas testing and emergency arrangements. In the morning several crews queue at the permit desk at once.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.215.1(2): work permit or master tag system in PEng-certified complex group procedures

evidence.note: Work permit or master tag system required for complex group control; queue time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Crew signs on and locks onto the lock box
steps.description: Each crew member signs the permit and puts a personal lock on the group lock box, so the isolations cannot be removed until they take it off. Contractors do the same with company-issued locks.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.214 and s.215(4): personal locks on the key-securing system

evidence.note: Same activity as gen-gas-routine-maintenance s15 and s17.

steps.name: Permit stays open while work proceeds
steps.description: The permit and isolations stay in place while the crew does the work under gas-routine-maintenance or the outage; no permit work is done in this interval, but the isolated equipment is unavailable to operations.

next.condition: work runs past a shift change

evidence.note: Duration of routine jobs from a few hours to about ten days; estimate.

steps.name: Revalidate permit at shift change
steps.description: At shift change the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors walk through open permits, confirm isolations are intact and transfer control of locks for workers who have gone home, recording the handover on the permit.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.214.1(4): lock control handed to a supervisor at shift change or reassignment

steps.name: Crew removes personal locks and signs off
steps.description: When the job is finished and tools are cleared, each crew member removes their personal lock from the lock box and the crew lead signs the permit off as work complete, stating whether the equipment is ready to test.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.215.3(1): only the worker who placed a lock removes it

steps.name: Confirm all workers clear and cancel permit
steps.description: The shift supervisor checks the lock box is empty and every signed-on worker is accounted for, then cancels the permit so the isolations can be removed. A lock left on blocks cancellation.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.215.3(3): isolation removed only when each worker is accounted for

next.condition: a personal lock is still on

steps.name: Trace a lock left on and authorise removal
steps.description: The supervisor phones the worker whose lock is still on, or their supervisor or contractor, and if the worker cannot return, confirms they are off site, records the reason and authorises cutting the lock.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 s.215.3(2): removal by a designated supervisor when the worker is unavailable

evidence.note: Share of permits with an abandoned lock is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Remove isolations and restore the line-up
steps.description: A field operator removes the locks and tags in reverse order, opens and closes valves to the normal line-up, closes drains and vents and racks breakers back in where operators are allowed to, ticking each point off.

error.defect_description: A valve left closed or a breaker left out.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Return equipment to service from the control room
steps.description: The control room operator returns the equipment to auto or standby on the DCS, starts it if required for the post-maintenance test, and confirms flows, pressures and alarms are normal.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Return locks and close the permit record
steps.description: The field operator hangs the locks and tags back on the lock board, records the time of restoration in the permit system and files the paper isolation record with the permit for audit.

error.defect_description: Permit record left open or incomplete.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Audit a sample of closed permits
steps.description: A safety advisor picks a sample of closed and open permits each week, checks signatures, isolation records and lock lists against the procedure, and visits open jobs to check locks in the field. Findings go to the plant manager.

control.basis: Company permit-to-work procedure: periodic permit audits

evidence.note: Audit share and minutes are estimates.

exceptions.name: New isolation list
exceptions.description: No stored isolation list exists, so the coordinator writes one from drawings.

exceptions.name: Isolation list rejected
exceptions.description: The shift supervisor finds an error and returns the list.

exceptions.name: Zero-energy test fails
exceptions.description: A passing valve or residual pressure means more isolation is needed.

exceptions.name: Multi-shift job
exceptions.description: The permit is revalidated and lock control handed over at shift change.

exceptions.name: Lock left on
exceptions.description: A worker left a personal lock on; the supervisor traces them or authorises removal.

exceptions.name: Deferred request
exceptions.description: The job needs the unit offline or conflicts with other open permits.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from permit request to permit record closed
benchmarks.population: Routine permits at a thermal generating plant, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: next-day preparation, a job of hours to a few days and same- or next-shift restoration. No published figure found.

pain_points.description: Several crews queue at the permit desk at the start of day shift while one supervisor issues and briefs permits, so craft time is lost before work starts.

evidence.note: Common observation in thermal plants; estimate.

pain_points.description: Writing isolation lists from drawings takes an experienced operator an hour or more, and outdated drawings or templates are a source of missed isolation points.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Locks left on by workers who have gone home hold equipment out of service until the worker is traced or a supervisor authorises removal.

evidence.note: The rule for removal is s.215.3; the frequency is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Outage seasons multiply the number of open permits and isolations that operators must track while also running the other units.

evidence.note: Organisation file surge; estimate.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code, Part 15: Managing the Control of Hazardous Energy (consolidated text)
sources.supports: s.212 equipment must be stopped and energy isolated with secured energy-isolating devices before work; s.213 worker tests and confirms the equipment is inoperative before starting; s.214 personal locks with unique identification and a written list of lock holders; s.214.1 each worker secures with own lock, control handed to a supervisor at shift change or reassignment; s.215 group control: supervisor or designated worker secures devices and keys, verifies isolation and posts a report at the work site, each worker locks onto the key-securing system; s.215.1 complex group control procedures certified by a professional engineer, including a work permit or master tag system and separate activation and verification roles; s.215.3 locks removed only by the worker who placed them or a designated supervisor, and only once each worker is accounted for. The text opened is the current consolidation (amended in 2023); the 2019-2022 text had the same section structure.

sources.title: Permit Coordinator job details (Wabamun, AB)
sources.supports: TransAlta has advertised a role titled Permit Coordinator at its Wabamun-area plant. The page opened shows only the title and that the position is filled; it does not show the duties, and it dates from after the reference period.

assumptions: Isolation is under complex group control (OHS Code s.215.1) with a work permit and group lock box, the usual method for multi-point steam plant isolations; simple single-lock jobs are not separated out.

A day-shift permit coordinator is added as a role the organisation file lacks; without it, isolation list preparation would fall on shift supervisors and field operators, adding about 5 FTE to their load.
The control room operator takes part in isolation and return to service although the organisation file does not list that role for this process.
Step s13 is the time the permit stays open while the work happens in another process; it holds no labour here.
Crew sign-on (s12) and sign-off (s15) duplicate time counted in gen-gas-routine-maintenance s15 and s17.
Field operator touch counts one operator; on large isolations two operators work together and the minutes would double.
The simulated 90th percentile (about 5 days) is narrower than the estimate of 9 days because triangular job durations at s13 understate the long tail of multi-week jobs held under one permit.
